sections.h2: Where do you record a deed in Stone County, Missouri?
sections.html:
Deeds for Stone County property are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office at 108-A East Fourth Street in Galena, the county seat. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the phone number is 417-357-6362. Amy Larson is the elected Recorder.

The office keeps the land records for the whole county, including Kimberling City, Reeds Spring, Crane, Hurley and Blue Eye. It also files federal and state liens, military discharge papers (DD-214) and marriage license information. Marriage license applications are by appointment only, so call before you drive in.

The county says its in-office records go back to 1851, which matches the year Stone County was organized. Records are searchable online from January 1, 1993 to the present through the county's iCounty portal at stonemo.icounty.com.

sections.h2: What does the Stone County Recorder charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
Ask the office for the exact total at 417-357-6362 before you mail or carry in a deed. The statute sets a base of $5 for the first page and $3 for each page after it. State user fees are added on top of that base.

Missouri changed those add-on fees in 2026. The Recorder published a notice that a flat $2.00 increase took effect statewide on August 28, 2026 under Senate Bill 938, covering recorded documents, marriage licenses and surveys or plats. That date has passed, so any older price list you find online may be short by $2.

Stone County recorder charges set in Missouri law, RSMo 59.310
ServiceAmount in the statute
Recording a deed or instrument$5 first page, $3 each added page
Copy of a recorded instrumentUp to $2 first page, $1 each added page
Certificate and seal$1
Release or assignment of several items$5 for each item beyond the first
Document that misses the format rulesExtra $25
Subdivision plat sheet$25 per sheet

Because the statute figures exclude the state user fees and the 2026 increase, the amount you actually pay is higher than anything in the table.

sections.h2: What format does a deed need before the Recorder accepts it?
sections.html:
A deed that breaks the format rules can still be recorded, but it costs $25 more or may be sent back. Missouri law lets the Recorder refuse a document that does not meet the page standards, and a refused document comes back with a written reason.

  • One or more separate pages, printed on one side, not bound and not on a continuous form.
  • Type no smaller than eight-point, in black or dark ink, on white or light paper of at least twenty-pound weight.
  • A top margin of at least three inches on the first page and three-quarters of an inch on every other edge.
  • Each signer's name typed or printed under the signature.

The first page, below the three-inch margin, has to show the document title, its date, every grantor's name and marital status, every grantee's name, any statutory addresses and the legal description. A deed also needs a mailing address for one of the grantees, and the Recorder will not record it without that address or the legal description.

sections.h2: How do recorded deeds in Stone County feed the property tax bill?
sections.html:
The County Assessor draws and updates parcel lines from the warranty deeds the Recorder sends over, so a deed that never gets recorded leaves the tax map out of date. The Assessor is Matt Daugherty, whose office is at 106 East Fifth Street in Galena. Real estate questions go to 417-357-6145.

The Assessor typically closes the assessment books by July 1, and the taxing districts normally set their rates by September 1. The Assessor does not set rates.

The Collector bills and takes payment. Anna Burk holds that office at the Historic Courthouse, 108 East Fourth Street, phone 417-357-6124. The Collector's page announced that 2026 tax statements would be mailed on Friday, November 13, 2026, with online payment opening November 6. Payment is due by December 31, and unpaid bills become delinquent on January 1. A mailed payment needs a postmark on or before December 31. Card payments carry a fee of 2.4 percent or a $1.95 minimum, and there is a drop box at the north entrance of the courthouse.

sections.h2: What does the Census Bureau show for Stone County housing?
sections.html:
Stone County had an estimated 32,503 residents on July 1, 2025, up 4.6 percent from the April 2020 base of 31,079. Owners live in 83.3 percent of homes, and the median value of an owner-occupied home was $249,000 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent was $896.

Residents aged 65 and older make up 33.3 percent of the population, the highest share of Stone, Warren and Webster counties. The Census counts 21,225 housing units but only 13,530 households, and the difference is homes that are not a household's usual residence. Owners of a second home sell through the same recording and tax offices as everyone else.

Public school districts serving the county include Blue Eye R-V, Crane R-III, Galena R-II, Hurley R-I and Reeds Spring R-IV, plus the Shell Knob 78 elementary district. Which district a house sits in decides part of its tax bill, and the Collector's statement shows it.

sections.h2: How can a Stone County owner avoid paying too much for a copy of a deed?
sections.html:
Order the copy straight from the Recorder. The office has warned residents about private companies that mail letters offering an official copy of a deed for $87 or more. Those firms simply request the document from the county and pass it along at a markup.

Most owners already hold the deed they received at closing, and the state fee cap for a copy is $2 for the first page and $1 for each page after it, plus $1 for a certificate. DeedWatch.com also offers a free property fraud alert that emails you when a document is recorded under a name or address you choose. The Recorder notes that it does not stop fraud but gives early warning.

faqs.q: Does Stone County record deeds online?
faqs.a: Searching is online. The county lists records from January 1, 1993 forward on its iCounty portal, and older records are kept in the Galena office. Call 417-357-6362 to ask how the office wants a new deed delivered, since the online portal is for searching.

faqs.q: What is the Stone County Recorder of Deeds address?
faqs.a: The office is at 108-A East Fourth Street, Galena, MO 65656. Hours are Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the phone is 417-357-6362.

Yes. A flat $2.00 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 took effect on August 28, 2026, and it applies to recorded documents, marriage licenses and plats or surveys. Ask the Recorder for the page-by-page total on your deed.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed has the wrong margins?
faqs.a: The Recorder can reject it and return it with a reason, or accept it for an extra $25. The first page needs a three-inch top margin, and the other edges need three-quarters of an inch.

faqs.q: Who do I call about the property tax bill after the sale?
faqs.a: Call the Stone County Collector at 417-357-6124. The 2026 statements were mailed November 13, 2026, taxes are due by December 31, and the Collector can tell you who the bill is addressed to.
